title: Penile Trauma (US / Doppler)

blocks.x: [e.g., Acute penile pain/swelling during intercourse, blunt trauma, urethral bleeding]
High-frequency linear transducer (7.5–15 MHz) gray-scale and color/spectral Doppler sonography of the penile shaft, base, and perineum performed in transverse and longitudinal planes.
Right Corpus Cavernosum: Homogeneous echotexture without focal hematoma, cavernosal tear, or intracavernosal mass.
Left Corpus Cavernosum: Homogeneous echotexture without focal hematoma or disruption.
Tunica Albuginea: Continuous, intact thin echogenic line surrounding both corpora cavernosa throughout the shaft and crura. No focal defect or contour deformity.
Corpus Spongiosum: Normal homogeneous echogenicity without disruption or hematoma.
Anterior Urethra: Intact walls without periurethral fluid collection, extravasation, or intraluminal thrombus.
Subcutaneous Tissues: Normal thickness; no subcutaneous or sub-Buck's hematoma, edema, or fluid collection.
Suspensory Ligament & Dorsal Vein Complex: Intact without thrombosis or rupture.
Cavernosal Arteries: Patent bilaterally with normal symmetric systolic and diastolic waveforms. No pseudoaneurysm or arteriovenous fistula (AVF).
Dorsal Penile Arteries & Deep Dorsal Vein: Patent with normal flow signals; no luminal thrombus or non-compressibility.
[Urgent surgical/urological alert if tunical tear, urethral injury, or vascular lesion is present]

bank.title: 2. Penile Fracture (Tunica Albuginea Rupture with Buck's Fascia Hematoma)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute snapping sound, severe pain, immediate detumescence, and "eggplant deformity" during sexual intercourse.

subs.title: Findings
items: Tunica Albuginea: There is a discrete 1.1 cm full-thickness focal discontinuity/defect in the ventral aspect of the right tunica albuginea at the mid-shaft, associated with localized contour irregularity.

Hematoma: Adjacent to the tunical defect, there is a large, heterogeneous, predominantly hypoechoic hematoma measuring 3.4 x 1.8 x 2.2 cm confined beneath Buck's fascia, exerting mild mass effect on the right corpus cavernosum.
Corpus Spongiosum: Intact, though mildly displaced leftward by the adjacent hematoma.
Vascularity: Bilateral cavernosal arteries remain patent without pseudoaneurysm.

subs.title: Impression
items: Right mid-shaft penile fracture, evidenced by a 1.1 cm focal rupture of the ventral tunica albuginea and an associated sub-Buck's fascia hematoma.
Intact corpus spongiosum. Urgent urological surgical consultation recommended.

bank.title: 3. Penile Fracture with Associated Urethral / Corpus Spongiosum Injury

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Penile trauma with gross hematuria and blood at the urethral meatus.

subs.title: Findings
items: There is a 1.4 cm disruption of the ventral tunica albuginea involving the left corpus cavernosum at the proximal shaft, accompanied by a large heterogeneous hematoma extending across the midline beneath Colles' fascia into the scrotal root ("butterfly hematoma").

The adjacent ventral aspect of the corpus spongiosum demonstrates focal architectural disruption and a surrounding periurethral fluid/blood collection containing tiny echogenic gas foci, concerning for concomitant urethral laceration.

subs.title: Impression
items: Left proximal penile fracture with extracapsular hematoma extending into the perineum.

Focal disruption of the corpus spongiosum with periurethral fluid and gas foci, highly suspicious for associated anterior urethral injury. Urgent urological evaluation and retrograde urethrography (RUG) advised.

bank.title: 4. Intracavernosal Hematoma Without Tunical Rupture (False Penile Fracture)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute penile pain and localized swelling during intercourse; rule out tunical tear.

subs.title: Findings
items: Within the mid-to-distal left corpus cavernosum, there is a well-circumscribed, oval, heterogeneous hypoechoic collection measuring 1.9 x 1.1 cm representing an isolated intracavernosal hematoma, with no internal color Doppler flow.
Careful multiplanar scanning confirms that the overlying echogenic tunica albuginea is completely intact and continuous without focal defect or extracapsular hematoma.

subs.title: Impression
items: Isolated left intracavernosal hematoma without sonographic evidence of tunica albuginea rupture.
Intact corpus spongiosum and normal penile Doppler vascularity.

bank.title: 5. Traumatic High-Flow Priapism (Cavernosal Artery Pseudoaneurysm / Arterio-Cavernosal Fistula)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Persistent, painless partial erection 48 hours following straddle injury to the perineum.

subs.title: Findings
items: Gray-scale imaging of the right proximal corpus cavernosum at the crural level demonstrates a focal 1.3 cm anechoic/hypoechoic outpouching surrounded by mild parenchymal heterogeneity.

Color Doppler demonstrates swirling bidirectional flow ("yin-yang sign") within the lesion, and spectral Doppler confirms a turbulent, high-velocity, low-resistance jet communicating directly between the right cavernosal artery and the cavernosal sinusoidal space (PSV = 115 cm/s, RI = 0.42).

subs.title: Impression
items: Traumatic right cavernosal artery pseudoaneurysm with an arterio-cavernosal fistula, diagnostic of post-traumatic high-flow (non-ischemic) priapism. Interventional radiology consultation for selective arterial embolization is recommended.

bank.title: 6. Superficial Dorsal Vein Rupture (Mimicking Penile Fracture)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute penile shaft swelling and ecchymosis following vigorous intercourse; no snapping sound or immediate detumescence.

subs.title: Findings
items: Both corpora cavernosa, the corpus spongiosum, and the entire circumference of the tunica albuginea are completely intact and unremarkable.

Within the dorsal subcutaneous tissue superficial to Buck's fascia, there is a localized 2.5 x 1.2 cm echogenic hematoma centered along the course of the superficial dorsal penile vein, with absence of normal venous Doppler flow at the site of injury.
The deep dorsal vein and dorsal arteries remain patent.

subs.title: Impression
items: Rupture of the superficial dorsal penile vein with an associated subcutaneous dorsal hematoma.
Intact tunica albuginea and corpora cavernosa; no evidence of penile fracture.

bank.title: 7. Mondor's Disease of the Penis (Superficial Dorsal Vein Thrombosis)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Palpable, painful cord-like induration along the dorsal penile shaft following repetitive microtrauma.

subs.title: Findings
items: Along the dorsal midline of the penile shaft superficial to Buck's fascia, the superficial dorsal penile vein is distended, non-compressible, and filled with echogenic intraluminal thrombus over a length of 4.5 cm.
Color and spectral Doppler demonstrate complete absence of intraluminal blood flow within the thrombosed segment, with mild surrounding perivenous hyperemia.
The tunica albuginea, corpora cavernosa, and deep dorsal vascular structures are normal.

subs.title: Impression
items: Thrombosis of the superficial dorsal penile vein (penile Mondor's disease).
Intact corpora cavernosa and normal deep penile vasculature.
